title: Quantitative characterization of the urine and serum metabolomes of children is essential for 'omics' studies.
ehr_evidence: Metabolomic data were generated from urine and serum biospecimens analyzed by LC-MS and NMR in European children recruited across six HELIX birth cohort study locations; no electronic or computerized health records were used.
summary: This commentary discusses the Lau et al. study that quantitatively characterized urine and serum metabolomes of European children and associated metabolites with BMI, diet, and demographics.
key_findings: The commentary highlights the Lau et al. finding of a novel association between urinary 4-deoxyerythronic acid and body mass index, suggesting the threonine metabolic pathway as a target for future obesity and type 2 diabetes studies.
Metabolite concentrations were associated with age, sex, BMI, and dietary intake and correlated within and between urine and serum biofluids.
captured_features: serum metabolome (Biocrates Absolute IDQ p180 kit, 177 metabolites)
study_design: Commentary on a cohort study (HELIX six longitudinal birth cohorts)
population: European children across six birth cohort study locations (HELIX)
exposure_domain: early-life exposome (diet, demographics, geographical location, environmental exposures)
limitations: The Biocrates p180 kit is not a comprehensive characterization of the metabolome and would require multiple analytical platforms and sample preparations.
Many differentiating metabolites remain unidentified and cannot be linked to metabolic pathways or genomic/proteomic data.
